answer: Registration difficulty should breathe with the tide of new identities. Each epoch, the network maintains an atlas of where fresh accounts cluster — by hosting provider, ASN, and funding-graph overlap. When arrivals surge above a learned baseline, the proof-of-work gate for minting a new identity hardens, and per-cluster weight caps tighten: every validator carries the same whisper, so a fee jump lands on all clones at once. Honest solo entrants barely feel the shift; a mass-registered fleet pays super-linearly as its whole tide gets repriced.
